title: Definitions
description: Defines proposal, promise, consideration, agreement, reciprocal promises, void and voidable contracts.

title: What agreements are contracts
description: All agreements are contracts if made by free consent of competent parties for lawful consideration and lawful object, and are not expressly declared void.

title: Who are competent to contract
description: Every person is competent to contract who is of age of majority, of sound mind, and not disqualified by law.

title: Consent
description: Two or more persons are said to consent when they agree upon the same thing in the same sense.

title: Free consent
description: Consent is free when not caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, or mistake.

title: Coercion
description: Coercion means committing or threatening to commit any act forbidden by IPC, or unlawful detaining or threatening to detain property, to cause a person to enter into an agreement.

title: Undue influence
description: A contract is induced by undue influence where one party is in a position to dominate the will of the other and uses that position to obtain unfair advantage.

title: Fraud
description: Fraud includes suggestion of untrue fact, active concealment, promise without intention to perform, or any act fitted to deceive.

title: Misrepresentation
description: Includes positive assertion not warranted by information, breach of duty causing advantage by misleading another, and innocent mistake causing agreement.

title: Voidability where consent caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation
description: When consent is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, contract is voidable at option of party whose consent was so caused.

title: What considerations and objects are lawful
description: Consideration or object is unlawful if forbidden by law, defeats legal provisions, is fraudulent, involves injury, or is immoral/opposed to public policy.

title: Agreements void if consideration and objects unlawful in part
description: If any part of a single consideration for one or more objects, or any one or any part of one of several considerations for a single object, is unlawful, agreement is void.

title: Agreement without consideration void
description: Agreement made without consideration is void subject to recognized statutory exceptions.

title: Agreement in restraint of trade void
description: Every agreement by which anyone is restrained from exercising lawful profession, trade or business is void, subject to statutory exceptions.

title: Agreements in restraint of legal proceedings void
description: Agreements absolutely restricting rights under or in respect of contract by usual legal proceedings are void.

title: Agreements void for uncertainty
description: Agreements the meaning of which is not certain or capable of being made certain are void.

title: Enforcement of contingent contracts
description: Contingent contracts to do or not do something if uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced until event has happened.

title: Obligation of parties to contracts
description: Parties to contract must either perform or offer to perform their respective promises unless performance dispensed with or excused.

title: Effect of refusal to perform promise wholly
description: When party refuses to perform or disables itself from performing promise in entirety, promisee may terminate unless signified acquiescence.

title: Effect of failure to perform at fixed time
description: When party promises to do certain thing at or before specified time and fails, contract may become voidable if time was of essence.
chapter: Chapter V - Certain Relations Resembling Contracts

title: Agreement to do impossible act
description: Agreement to do impossible act is void; contract to do act becomes void when act becomes impossible or unlawful after contract.
chapter: Chapter V - Certain Relations Resembling Contracts

title: Effect of novation, rescission and alteration
description: If parties substitute new contract, or rescind or alter it, original contract need not be performed.
chapter: Chapter VI - Of the Consequences of Breach

title: Promisee may dispense with or remit performance
description: Promisee may dispense with or remit wholly or in part performance of promise made to him, or extend time, or accept satisfaction.
chapter: Chapter VI - Of the Consequences of Breach

title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach
description: Party suffering by breach is entitled to compensation for loss or damage naturally arising in usual course of things or known to parties at contract formation.
chapter: Chapter VI - Of the Consequences of Breach

title: Compensation for breach where penalty stipulated
description: When contract names sum to be paid on breach or contains penalty stipulation, aggrieved party is entitled to reasonable compensation not exceeding amount named.
